blocks.title: Counting and De Morgan
blocks.md: For two sets, and the two laws of De Morgan (the complement of a union is the intersection of complements, and vice versa):
blocks.tex: n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B) \qquad (A \cup B)' = A' \cap B' \qquad (A \cap B)' = A' \cup B'

blocks.title: Three sets
blocks.md: The inclusion–exclusion principle for three sets. Always fill a Venn diagram from the **centre outwards** (A ∩ B ∩ C first):
blocks.tex: n(A \cup B \cup C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) - n(A \cap B) - n(B \cap C) - n(A \cap C) + n(A \cap B \cap C)

blocks.title: Logic
blocks.md: A **statement** is true or false. The negation ¬p reverses the truth value. For p ⇒ q (if p then q): the **converse** is q ⇒ p, the **contrapositive** is ¬q ⇒ ¬p (always equivalent to p ⇒ q), and p ⇒ q is false only when p is true and q is false.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Adding n(A) + n(B) without subtracting the overlap.
- Believing the converse is equivalent: 'if it rains the road is wet' does not mean 'if the road is wet it rained'.
- Forgetting the elements outside all the circles (the 'neither' region).

blocks.title: Example 1: two sets
blocks.statement: In a class of 60 students, 35 play football (F), 28 play volleyball (V) and 10 play both. How many play neither?
steps: Regions: only F = 25, both = 10, only V = 18, neither = 7: total 60.

blocks.title: Example 2: three sets
blocks.statement: Of 50 pupils, n(A) = 22, n(B) = 20, n(C) = 18, n(A∩B) = 8, n(B∩C) = 6, n(A∩C) = 7 and n(A∩B∩C) = 3. How many are in none of the sets? Then write the contrapositive of 'if x > 3 then x² > 9'.
steps: Contrapositive: 'if x² ≤ 9 then x ≤ 3'. It is true for x > 3 ⇒ x² > 9.
blocks.answer: **8 pupils; contrapositive: if x² ≤ 9 then x ≤ 3.**

Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: The contrapositive of 'if a number is divisible by 4 then it is even' is:
choices: a number is even or divisible by 4
if a number is not even then it is not divisible by 4
if a number is even then it is divisible by 4
if a number is not divisible by 4 then it is not even
exercises.explanation: Negate and swap both parts. The first wrong option is the converse, the second the inverse.
